title: Identity resolution and record merge for Riverview patient records
subtitle: Scored links across ChartLine, MedHarbor, and SiteNotes. Never auto-merge on name alone. Human queue 0.62-0.84.
author: Aman Kumar
team: Clinical Integration / Patient API (Northstar at Riverview Health Network)
audience: Priya Nair (EM), Dr. Anita Shah (CMIO liaison), Kavya Menon (backend), Luis Ortega (interfaces), Sneha Iyer (QA), Chris Patel (data), Phoenix HIM
owners: Aman Kumar (design/service), Kavya Menon (UI + API view), Luis Ortega (privacy ticket + hold lists), Sneha Iyer (labeled fixtures), Priya Nair (automerge gate)
summary: Design for identity-merge, a Python service that scores and (narrowly) links per-facility patient records. Last+DOB+sex is a blocking key, not a matcher. Tokenized last-4 SSN and ChartLine mother's maiden are score features pending privacy review. Auto-merge is off until a labeled set exists. Humans handle 0.62-0.84. Over-merge is treated as worse than under-merge.
form_description: Technical design for Riverview record merge and identity resolution, written for engineering, HIM, and the CMIO liaison before any auto-link is enabled.
revision_history: Notes from Shah privacy huddle. Twin fixture called out.
Killed payload-hash person_key after Kavya spike review. Added survivorship order.
Approved for schema work. FEATURE_SSN_TOKEN and FEATURE_AUTOMERGE remain off.

blocks.text: 1. Decision

We will stand up a Python service `identity-merge` that proposes, and in a narrow band auto-applies, links between per-facility patient records across ChartLine, MedHarbor, and SiteNotes. The Patient Chart API (RVH-PRD-2020-019) still keys charts by (facility_id, local_mrn). This service sits beside it. It writes match tables in Postgres, not into the EMRs. It never write-backs a merged id to ChartLine. Priya Nair started as EM on January 11, three days ago, and asked for a design she can defend in Shah's Thursday privacy huddle. This is that design.

Auto-merge only when score >= 0.85 and the pair is not in a hold list. Human queue for 0.62-0.84. Below 0.62 we store the pair as unmatched and do not show a yellow chip. Never auto-merge on name alone, not even on last+DOB+sex. That rule is how Cottonwood welded two people in Luis Ortega's v17 spreadsheet, and it is how Mesa Ridge twins collapsed into one RapidChart header during the December 9 fixture run. Sneha Iyer still has that fixture. We will keep it as a permanent reject case.

blocks.label: Decision requested
blocks.text: Approve match tables on pg-patient-01, a scored linker that uses last+DOB+sex as a blocking key only, and extra tokens (last-4 SSN hashed, ChartLine mother's maiden hashed) as score features. Human queue in identity-merge-ui for 0.62-0.84. Legal/privacy review of the SSN token remains open with Luis Ortega as owner. Do not ship auto-merge until that review returns.

Rejected alternative: keep the spreadsheet and a nightly script that dumps `mrn_xwalk_v17_FINAL_use_this.xlsx` into `id_hint.possible_match`. Chris Patel offered to warehouse-clean it. That died because the file has 1,204 blank rows, 88 last+DOB collisions, and no audit of who merged whom. Also rejected: auto-merge at 0.70 to 'clear the queue' before RapidChart's Phoenix ED flag. Clearing a queue of identity links is how you create a different incident. Under-merge costs clicks. Over-merge costs the wrong penicillin allergy. We take clicks.
2. Why last+DOB+sex is not a matcher

The v0 API uses last name + DOB + sex as a stub score of 0.55 and calls the result `possible_matches`. That was honest about being a stub. It is not honest as a merger. Riverview has three documented collision classes. First, twins. Mesa Ridge ChartLine has at least 14 twin pairs with the same last name, same DOB, opposite or same sex. Four of those pairs are same-sex twins. Second, the 2014 ChartLine conversion at Cottonwood and Show Low reused a six-digit MRN block. Local MRN 100442 is a living person at Cottonwood and a 2013 deceased record that still answers GetPatient at Show Low with a similar last name. Third, hyphenated last names that ChartLine truncates at 20 characters and MedHarbor stores full. Last-name equality is not last-name equality.

Denise Howell already treats the yellow chip as noise at Flagstaff because the stub fires on too many transfers from Phoenix Central. If we auto-merge those, RapidChart will assemble Phoenix allergies onto a Flagstaff stay that is a different human. Shah's words in the January 8 huddle: stop guessing. A human in HIM (health information management) can guess with a chart in front of them. A service can only apply rules we can explain later.
If your score cannot tell me why two records are the same person, I will not let you glue their allergies together. I do not care that the queue is long.
blocks.attrib: Dr. Anita Shah, January 8 2021 privacy huddle

blocks.text: Partial sync is a known smell from the census path Chris Patel runs into CensusMart. When a facility feed lags, the warehouse upserts the same encounter as if it were new because the lagging feed misses the natural key. Identity-merge will see the same shape: a ChartLine person arriving twice, hours apart, with a slightly different first name because a registration clerk fixed a typo. If we treat every upsert as a new person we under-merge. If we treat every similar name as the same person we over-merge. The match tables have to remember that we already decided a pair, including decided-no.
3. Constraints

items: No write-back to ChartLine, MedHarbor, or SiteNotes. Links live in our Postgres. EMRs keep their MRNs.

Patient Chart API remains the read path. identity-merge does not serve RapidChart directly. It updates match tables the API reads for `possible_matches` and, after a confirmed merge, for `linked_ids`.
PHI: last-4 SSN never stored in the clear. Mother's maiden never stored in the clear. We store HMAC-SHA256 with a key in `/etc/identity-merge/hmac.key` on the PHI VLAN hosts only.
Legal/privacy review of even the tokenized last-4 is pending. Owner: Luis Ortega. Until that returns, the SSN feature weight is compiled out (`FEATURE_SSN_TOKEN=0`).
Human reviewers are HIM staff at Phoenix Central plus a Flagstaff backup. They are not nurses. Denise Howell will not be asked to merge records on a night shift.
Never auto-merge on name alone. Name features may raise a score. They cannot cross 0.85 without a second independent token (DOB+sex is not independent of the blocking key).
Service is Python 3.8, same runtime as patient-api, deployed to `idm-01.flagstaff.riverview.internal` and `idm-02.phx.riverview.internal`.

blocks.text: 4. Data model

All match state lives in database `patient_api` on `pg-patient-01.flagstaff.riverview.internal`, schema `idm`. We did not create a second cluster. Diego Alvarez does not want another WAL to back up on the PHI VLAN. We did create a second role `identity_merge` that can write `idm.*` and cannot write `chart_audit.*`. The API role can read `idm.link` and `idm.queue` and cannot write them. Break that direction and we will have the API 'helpfully' merging on assemble, which is how you get an incident at 07:10 change of shift.

-- schema idm on pg-patient-01, database patient_api
CREATE TABLE idm.person_token (
  person_key      text PRIMARY KEY,           -- hmac(facility||source||local_mrn)
  facility_id     text NOT NULL,
  source          text NOT NULL,              -- chartline|medharbor|sitenotes
  local_mrn       text NOT NULL,              -- stored; this table is PHI
  last_norm       text NOT NULL,
  first_norm      text,
  dob             date NOT NULL,
  sex_norm        text NOT NULL,              -- F/M/U/X
  ssn4_hmac       text,                       -- nullable; FEATURE_SSN_TOKEN
  maiden_hmac     text,                       -- nullable; ChartLine only
  token_version   integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  source_updated  timestamptz NOT NULL,
  ingested_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (facility_id, source, local_mrn)
);
CREATE INDEX person_token_block_ix ON idm.person_token (last_norm, dob, sex_norm);

CREATE TABLE idm.pair (
  pair_id         bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  left_key        text NOT NULL REFERENCES idm.person_token(person_key),
  right_key       text NOT NULL REFERENCES idm.person_token(person_key),
  score           numeric(4,3) NOT NULL,
  features        jsonb NOT NULL,             -- which tokens hit, weights
  state           text NOT NULL,              -- unmatched|queued|linked|rejected|hold
  decided_by      text,                       -- actor or 'auto'
  decided_at      timestamptz,
  UNIQUE (left_key, right_key),
  CHECK (left_key < right_key)
);

CREATE TABLE idm.link (
  link_id         bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  surviving_key   text NOT NULL,
  member_key      text NOT NULL,
  pair_id         bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES idm.pair(pair_id),
  UNIQUE (member_key)
);

CREATE TABLE idm.queue (
  pair_id         bigint PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES idm.pair(pair_id),
  enqueued_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  facility_hint   text,
  reason          text NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE idm.hold (
  person_key      text PRIMARY KEY,
  reason          text NOT NULL,
  set_by          text NOT NULL,
  set_at          timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
blocks.caption: Match tables. person_token is PHI. pair.features must not include raw SSN or maiden, only booleans like ssn4_hit.

blocks.text: Survivorship is recorded on `idm.link.surviving_key`. The surviving record is the one RapidChart will title. Members still exist; we do not delete tokens. Un-merge is an insert of a new pair state `rejected` plus delete from `idm.link`. We do not update history out of existence. Shah asked for a story she can tell medical records when a patient complains. The story is: here is the pair_id, here is who decided, here is the score, here is the unlink time.
4.1 Survivorship rules
When auto-merge or a human confirms a link, pick a survivor with these rules, in order. First source wins only as a last resort, because ChartLine is not always righter, it is just older.

items: If exactly one member has a current inpatient encounter, that member is the survivor. RapidChart should title the person who is in a bed today.

If both or neither are inpatient, prefer ChartLine over MedHarbor over SiteNotes when the ChartLine token's `source_updated` is within 400 days. ChartLine registration is still the legal chart at eight of eleven facilities.
If ChartLine is stale (>400 days) and MedHarbor has a later `source_updated`, MedHarbor wins. This is the Flagstaff clinic remnant case.
If the pair includes a hold key, do not auto-apply. Queue even if score is 0.99.
Never survive a deceased ChartLine shell over a living MedHarbor record solely because ChartLine is 'primary.' Deceased flag is a veto on survival unless both are deceased.
On conflict (both inpatient at different facilities, which happens on transfers), do not auto-merge. Queue with reason `dual_inpatient`. HIM calls both units.

blocks.text: Chris Patel wanted survivorship to follow warehouse `dim_patient.master_id` so census and RapidChart agree. That dim is built from the same spreadsheet we are replacing, and it is 6.4h stale. If we follow it we import the twins. Census can read `idm.link` later. Census does not get to vote in v1.
5. Scoring

Blocking key is (last_norm, dob, sex_norm). We only compare pairs that share a block, plus a small extra set: same ssn4_hmac even if last_norm differs (hyphen / truncation), and same maiden_hmac plus dob. That extra set is how we catch ChartLine truncation. We do not compare all 1.8M tokens to all 1.8M tokens. Full join is how you take down pg-patient-01. Luis counted 1.84M distinct (facility, source, mrn) keys across the three EMRs as of January 6, 2021. Blocks of last+dob+sex have a p95 size of 3 and a max of 41 (a very common last name plus a 1980s DOB cluster). Max 41 is fine. If a block exceeds 80 we skip auto-score and queue the whole block as `wide_block`.

rows: last_norm exact (inside block it is always 1)
Blocking only. Does not add score.
Typos, nicknames still fail this. Good.
Compiled out until Luis's review lands.
ChartLine-only field, 71% at Sierra Vista, 18% at Phoenix.
2014 reuse smell. Do not treat as evidence.
When both sources have a phone. Often missing.
Score still stored for the reviewer.
blocks.caption: Base score starts at 0.50 for any blocked pair (they already share last+DOB+sex). Features add or subtract. Cap at 0.99. Floor at 0.05.

blocks.text: Worked examples. Twin pair at Mesa Ridge, same last, same DOB, same sex, different first, both ChartLine, no SSN on file, no maiden. Base 0.50 + first JW 0.04 = 0.54. Unmatched. Good. Cottonwood 100442 vs Show Low 100442, last names similar after truncation, DOB off by one year because the 2014 conversion defaulted missing DOB to 1/1/1900 on the deceased shell. They do not share a block (DOB differs). Extra set does not fire (no ssn4). Unmatched. Also good. Flagstaff clinic remnant: ChartLine FLG 448291 and MedHarbor FLG 88211, same last, same DOB, same sex, maiden hit, phone hit. Base 0.50 + first 0.12 + maiden 0.22 + phone 0.16 = 1.00 capped 0.99. Auto-merge if SSN feature is off and no hold. This is the case RapidChart actually needs.

If FEATURE_SSN_TOKEN is still 0 when we go live, auto-merge volume will be small. That is acceptable. The queue will be large. HIM at Phoenix Central has 2.5 FTE assigned per Rahul. They clear about 40 pairs/hour when the UI is not terrible. I would rather a 3-week queue than a wrong link. Priya asked if we could 'tune 0.85 down to 0.78 to help.' No. 0.85 stays until we have a labeled set Sneha trusts. We do not have that set yet. We have 200 hand-labeled pairs from Luis's spreadsheet, which is the thing we do not trust. Circular.
6. Service behavior

`identity-merge` ingests person tokens from the same adapters patient-api uses. It does not call assemble. Assemble can partial-succeed; identity cannot. If ChartLine SOAP 504s we skip that facility for the run and leave `idm.person_token.source_updated` stale. Stale tokens stay in blocks. We do not delete them because a lagging feed is how partial sync created duplicate census rows, and we are not repeating that pattern with identity. Ingest is incremental on `source_updated`. Full rebuild is a command, not a schedule: `identity-merge rebuild --source chartline --facility CWD`. Cottonwood will need one after we load the 2014 reuse hold list.
Run loop

items: Pull new/updated registrations from each adapter since last high-water mark (Redis key `idm:hw:{source}:{facility}`).

Normalize names (uppercase, strip punctuation, map Mc / Mac, cut ChartLine 20-char last to a second token `last_trunc20` for extra blocking). Hash SSN4 and maiden if features enabled and values present.
Upsert `idm.person_token`. If local_mrn changed meaning (rare, ChartLine merge-inside-EMR), write a hold and queue.
Score against the block and extra sets. Write `idm.pair` in states unmatched / queued / linked-candidate.
Auto-apply linked-candidate where score >= 0.85, neither on hold, not dual_inpatient, FEATURE_AUTOMERGE=1. Default FEATURE_AUTOMERGE=0 until Priya says otherwise.
Enqueue 0.62-0.84. Drop below 0.62 to unmatched. Do not re-enqueue a rejected pair unless a feature value changed (ssn4 appeared, maiden appeared, name changed).

# on idm-01.flagstaff.riverview.internal
sudo systemctl status identity-merge
journalctl -u identity-merge -n 80 --no-pager

# dry-run score a known twin fixture (no writes)
sudo -u identity-merge /opt/identity-merge/venv/bin/identity-merge score \
  --left FLG/chartline/448291 --right MESA/chartline/448292 --dry-run

# rebuild Cottonwood after hold list load
sudo -u identity-merge /opt/identity-merge/venv/bin/identity-merge rebuild \
  --source chartline --facility CWD --no-automerge

# queue dump for HIM (no names in stdout; keys only)
psql -h pg-patient-01.flagstaff.riverview.internal -U identity_merge -d patient_api \
  -c "select pair_id, score, reason, enqueued_at from idm.queue order by enqueued_at limit 25;"
blocks.caption: Commands for the person on call. Dry-run prints features and score. It does not print SSN or maiden.

blocks.text: API read path: patient-api already selects from `id_hint.possible_match`. We will point that view at `idm.pair` where state in (queued, linked) and score >= 0.62. Linked members also populate `linked_ids` on assemble so RapidChart can stop showing two cards after HIM confirms. Until FEATURE_AUTOMERGE is on, linked_ids only fills from human decisions. Kavya estimated the view swap at 1.4 days. Sneha owns contract tests that a linked pair does not union allergies until `state=linked`. Queued pairs stay yellow chips.
7. Human queue

UI is a small internal app `identity-merge-ui` on `idm-ui.phx.riverview.internal`, Phoenix Central HIM VLAN only. Reviewers see last, first, DOB, sex, facility, source, last 4 of MRN, encounter summary (class + admit_at, no diagnoses), and the feature hits as English: 'mother's maiden token matched', 'last-4 token matched', 'phones matched', 'same MRN digits at different facilities (penalty)'. They do not see raw SSN or maiden. They get three buttons: Link, Not the same, Hold. Hold requires a reason code. Link requires picking a survivor or accepting the recommended survivor. Every click writes `idm.pair.decided_by` as their employeeNumber.

Score band 0.62-0.84 is the queue. Why those numbers: on the 200-pair labeled slice, 0.85+ had 1 false link (the Cottonwood reuse with a coincidental phone), which is why same-MRN-different-facility is now a penalty and why FEATURE_AUTOMERGE starts off. 0.62-0.84 had 22 true links and 31 false. Humans can sort that. Below 0.62 had 2 true links, both hyphenation plus missing maiden. We will pick those up when maiden fill improves, not by lowering the floor. Sneha will grow the labeled set to 1,000 pairs before anyone talks about moving 0.85. Owner of the labeled set: Sneha. Owner of the UI: Kavya with HIM superuser Mara Ellison (Phoenix Central HIM, extra name, not in the Northstar world file, she sat in the January 8 huddle).

blocks.caption: Over-merge vs under-merge is the actual design fight. Guards are code or roles, not vibes.

blocks.text: Partial sync deserves its own paragraph because we already know the shape. CensusMart's nightly load upserts on a weak key when a facility file is late, then the late file arrives and a second row appears. Identity ingest must upsert on (facility_id, source, local_mrn) and must not create person_key from a hash that includes source_updated. If person_key includes a timestamp, every lag creates a new person. I wrote that sentence because Kavya's spike on January 12 hashed the whole adapter payload. We caught it in review. The spike is in `identity-merge/spikes/hash-payload` with a README that says do not. person_key = HMAC(facility || source || local_mrn).

Clock and lag: if Flagstaff ChartLine is 14 minutes behind (Yuma's feed did this on August 8, ChartLine can too), a registration clerk's name fix arrives late. We re-score on upsert. If the pair was rejected yesterday and first_norm changed, we re-enqueue. If it was linked, we do not unlink on a name fix. Unlink is human only. Auto-unmerge is how you flap RapidChart headers all morning.
9. Privacy review (open)

Luis Ortega owns the question: may we HMAC the last-4 SSN with a server-side key and store the digest on pg-patient-01. Shah is willing to hear yes if the digest cannot be reversed by HIM, by Northstar, or by a Tableau user. HMAC with a 32-byte key stored only on idm-01/idm-02 and pg-patient-01 (the key must not live in the EDW). Chris Patel will not get a replica of `idm.person_token`. That is a condition, not a preference. Mother's maiden is ChartLine-only and less regulated than SSN, but we treat it the same because it is still an identifier relatives know. Until Luis gets a written yes from privacy (ticket RVH-PRIV-2021-003), FEATURE_SSN_TOKEN stays 0 and the column stays null. Do not 'just hash it in staging to see.' Staging is a copy of PHI with a thinner firewall.

blocks.label: Open hold
blocks.text: Do not enable FEATURE_SSN_TOKEN or FEATURE_AUTOMERGE without Priya Nair plus Dr. Anita Shah on the thread. Luis can unblock the token. He cannot unblock auto-merge. Auto-merge is a clinical identity decision dressed up as a flag.
10. Rollout

items: Week of Jan 18: schema idm on pg-patient-01. Load CWD/SHLO reuse hold list from Luis (2,186 keys). FEATURE_AUTOMERGE=0, FEATURE_SSN_TOKEN=0.
Week of Jan 25: ingest ChartLine Flagstaff + Mesa only. Score. Do not touch RapidChart view. Sneha compares queue to the 200 labeled pairs.
Week of Feb 8: HIM UI to Mara's team with queued Flagstaff pairs only. Measure minutes per pair. Target under 1.7 min median.
Week of Feb 22: point patient-api possible_matches view at idm.pair for Flagstaff. Yellow chips should drop from 'dozens' to the queued band. Denise Howell watches for two weeks.
Privacy review RVH-PRIV-2021-003 due March 5 (Luis). If yes, enable FEATURE_SSN_TOKEN in staging, never in prod the same day.
FEATURE_AUTOMERGE remains off until labeled set >= 1000 and false-link at 0.85 is 0 on that set. Priya gates it.

blocks.text: Rollback: point the view back at `id_hint.possible_match`, set FEATURE_AUTOMERGE=0, leave tables in place. Do not DROP SCHEMA idm. Un-merge is a data problem if we have already linked. We will write `identity-merge unlink --pair-id` before go-live so on-call is not crafting SQL at 03:00.

blocks.text: 12. What this is not

This is not an EMPI product we sell. This is not a FHIR Patient $merge. This is not a nightly warehouse job. This is a small Python service, a handful of Postgres tables, a HIM queue, and a set of flags that default off. The Patient Chart API keeps serving (facility, local_mrn). When a link exists, assemble may add linked_ids and still must not union allergies until the link state is linked, not queued. If someone proposes matching on name alone 'just for the ED tracker,' the answer is the Mesa Ridge twin fixture and this document.

Related: RVH-PRD-2020-019, RVH-2109, RVH-PRIV-2021-003, Sneha twin fixture `fixtures/identity/mesa-twins.json`, Luis hold list `holds/cwd-shlo-2014-reuse.csv`. I will update scores when the labeled set hits 1,000. I will not update 0.85 because a demo looks better.
